old: \caption[Construction of the braided pneumatic actuator]{The construction the finite-element program of this section would represent. (A) Longitudinal section with loads and constraints: internal pressure acts inside-out on the elastomer bladder; the braided aramid sleeve, woven in two handed weaves, carries the tension and converts radial expansion to axial contraction; layer contact pairs act between bladder, sleeve, and caps; with the ends clamped in the Onyx or aluminum caps the pressurized actuator develops an axial force reacted at the fixed end; and the dash-dot centerline is the symmetry axis of the half-model. (B) Exploded half-cutaway of the layered construction, from inside out: the inner rubber tube, the two aramid helical reinforcement families of opposite handedness, the outer rubber, and the fabric covering, anchored at the sectioned end cap, with the open semicircular section marking the symmetry boundary of the half-model. Not to scale.}
new: \caption[Construction of the braided pneumatic actuator]{Construction represented by the proposed finite-element model. (A) Six idealized wall layers with contact interfaces, outward internal pressure, and a fixed cap end. Longitudinal symmetry permits in-plane expansion; at the transverse half-length boundary, axial displacement is fixed, or a movable boundary with an optional external load replaces transverse symmetry. (B) Illustrative exploded cutaway showing the fabric covering, rubber, and opposite-handed aramid reinforcement anchored at the cap. The plane callout identifies longitudinal symmetry; the rubber callout identifies retained material above it. The middle rubber layer is explicit in (A) but not separated in (B). Layer spacing and cap details are schematic. Not to scale.}

old: \caption[Five-stage training curriculum and stage scores]{The five-stage training curriculum. Each stage adds one capability and is seeded with the previous stage's winner, so only the newly activated pathway gains are searched; the chip fill tracks the preparation's support level from suspended air stepping through stance to ground. Scores are stage-appropriate and rhythm-gated where rhythm is the capability under test, and finalists at every stage must pass the perturbation and basin gates before the score is read.}
new: \caption[Five-stage training curriculum and stage scores]{The five-stage training curriculum.
